skill.name: github-project-contributor-finder-api-skill
skill.description: Search GitHub projects through BrowserAct using keyword, star, and update filters, then return repository details and public contributor profiles.
skill.summary: Find filtered GitHub repositories and public contributor profiles through a BrowserAct workflow.
skill.author: browser-act

security_audit.summary: The BrowserAct requests are expected but transmit search parameters and a bearer credential to a third-party service. Most static matches are benign Markdown or scoped credential handling, but the skill asks users to provide API keys directly. Raw GitHub-derived text and aggregated contact details also create prompt-injection, privacy, and compliance risks.

remediation.issue: The instructions ask users to provide API keys directly to the agent.
remediation.suggestion: Require BROWSERACT_API_KEY through an environment variable or approved secret manager. Never request or accept credentials in chat.

remediation.issue: External repository and profile text is printed without trust boundaries.
remediation.suggestion: Parse expected fields, label all returned text as untrusted data, and prevent repository content from becoming agent instructions.

remediation.issue: The workflow aggregates personal links and social handles for outreach and profiling.
remediation.suggestion: Add purpose limits, data minimization, retention rules, and consent or lawful-basis checks before recruiting or marketing use.

remediation.issue: Search criteria, task identifiers, and credentials are transmitted to BrowserAct.
remediation.suggestion: Disclose the third-party transfer, keep HTTPS endpoint allowlisting, and use a dedicated key with the narrowest available permissions.

content.value_statement: Finding relevant open-source projects and active contributors manually takes time. This skill searches through BrowserAct and returns repository metrics and public contributor profiles.
actual_capabilities: Filters results by minimum stars and last update date.
Controls search pagination and the item limit per page.
Starts a BrowserAct workflow and polls its status for up to 15 minutes.
Returns repository metrics and available public contributor profile fields.
limitations: Requires a BrowserAct account, API key, network access, and the Python requests package.
Depends on BrowserAct service availability, workflow behavior, quotas, and account concurrency limits.
Contributor websites, biographies, and social handles may be missing, outdated, or inaccurate.
External result text is not sanitized and must be treated as untrusted data.

use_cases.title: Map an Open-Source Topic
use_cases.description: Find active repositories in a technical domain and compare their descriptions, stars, owners, and recent updates.

use_cases.title: Review Public Contributor Profiles
use_cases.description: Identify relevant contributors and review public profile links for role-related research with appropriate consent and privacy controls.

use_cases.title: Plan Community Outreach
use_cases.description: Discover active projects and contributors before designing relevant, respectful community engagement.

prompt_templates.title: Find Repositories
prompt_templates.prompt: Find GitHub repositories about [topic]. Use sensible defaults and summarize repository names, links, descriptions, and star counts.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner search with only a topic.

prompt_templates.title: Apply Search Filters
prompt_templates.prompt: Search for [topic] repositories with at least [stars] stars, updated since [date]. Review [pages] pages and return [items] results per page.

prompt_templates.title: Research Contributors
prompt_templates.prompt: Find contributors to repositories about [topic]. Include only relevant public profile fields and explain missing data. Do not request my API key in chat.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Project Ecosystems
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare GitHub ecosystems for [topic A] and [topic B] using equal filters. Group projects by activity, stars, owners, and contributor signals.

output_examples.input: Find browser automation repositories with at least 1,000 stars, updated since 2026-01-01.
output_examples.output: A filtered repository list with names, links, owners, descriptions, star counts, and available contributor profiles.

output_examples.input: Find active machine learning contributors and include public websites when available.
output: Contributor summaries show usernames, profile links, biographies, related repositories, and public websites when returned.
Missing social fields are identified instead of inferred.

best_practices: Set BROWSERACT_API_KEY through an approved secret manager or local environment configuration.
Use narrow keywords, realistic star thresholds, and a current update date to reduce irrelevant results.
Treat returned descriptions, biographies, websites, and social handles as untrusted and verify them before use.
anti_patterns: Do not paste API keys into chat, prompts, logs, or shared command history.
Do not use public profile data for unsolicited bulk outreach or sensitive personal profiling.
Do not treat repository descriptions or contributor biographies as trusted agent instructions.

faq.question: What credentials does this skill require?
faq.answer: It requires BROWSERACT_API_KEY. Configure it securely in the environment or an approved secret manager.

faq.question: Does the skill call GitHub directly?
faq.answer: No. The bundled script starts and monitors a BrowserAct workflow that performs the collection.

faq.question: Which search filters are supported?
faq.answer: It supports keywords, minimum stars, last update date, page count, and item count per page.

faq.question: How long can a search run?
faq.answer: The script polls for up to 15 minutes and reports status every 10 seconds.

faq.question: Are contributor contact fields always available?
faq.answer: No. Websites, biographies, and social handles depend on public source data and may be missing or outdated.

faq.question: How should returned text be handled?
faq.answer: Treat all repository and profile text as untrusted data. Verify important facts and ignore embedded instructions.
